tcs.title: How we look after your data
content: CPCDS CONSUMER SOLUTIONS considers protecting the confidentiality and integrity of our customers' data to be one of the fundamental pillars of the relationship of trust with the people who use our services.

CPCDS CONSUMER SOLUTIONS has an appropriate organisation and processes in place to protect your data against destruction, alteration and unauthorised access.
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies to the processing of personal data wholly or partly by automated means, and to the processing other than by automated means of personal data that form part of a filing system.

We comply with the confidentiality obligations arising from our activity as a credit intermediary, under the applicable national legislation and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 — the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

faqs.title: What is the role of a mortgage broker in Portugal?
faqs.body: A mortgage broker in Portugal acts as an intermediary between borrowers and lenders. Their role is to help clients secure the best mortgage terms by evaluating their financial situation, comparing loan offers from various banks, and guiding them through the application process.

faqs.title: Why should I use a mortgage broker instead of going directly to a bank?
faqs.body: Mortgage brokers offer several advantages. They have access to a wide range of loan products and can provide expert guidance on the best options for your specific needs. Brokers can often secure more favourable terms and help streamline the application process, saving you time and money.

faqs.title: How do mortgage brokers get paid in Portugal?
faqs.body: Our mortgage brokerage services are entirely free for clients: under Bank of Portugal rules, we do not charge you for our assistance. We are paid a commission by the lending institution when a client's mortgage is approved, usually a percentage of the loan amount.

faqs.title: Are mortgage brokers regulated in Portugal?
faqs.body: Yes, mortgage brokers in Portugal are regulated by the Bank of Portugal (Banco de Portugal). To operate legally, brokers must be registered with and authorised by this regulatory authority. This ensures that brokers adhere to professional standards and ethical practices.

faqs.title: What factors affect mortgage interest rates in Portugal?
faqs.body: Mortgage interest rates in Portugal can be influenced by various factors, including the Eurozone's monetary policy, the property's location, the loan-to-value ratio, the borrower's creditworthiness, and market competition among lenders.

faqs.title: How can I improve my chances of getting a mortgage in Portugal?
faqs.body: To increase your likelihood of mortgage approval, maintain a good credit history, save for a sizeable down payment, provide accurate financial documentation, and work with a mortgage broker to identify lenders that match your financial profile.

faqs.title: What is the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratio for mortgages in Portugal?
faqs.body: The LTV ratio can vary, but it's common for lenders to offer mortgages with an LTV of up to 80% of the property's value. However, specific terms may vary based on your financial situation and the lending institution.

faqs.title: Can I get a mortgage in Portugal as a foreign investor or non-resident?
faqs.body: Yes, Portugal welcomes foreign investors, and non-residents can typically secure mortgages for property purchases. The requirements may vary, so it's advisable to work with a mortgage broker experienced in handling international clients.

faqs.title: How long does the mortgage approval process in Portugal usually take?
faqs.body: The mortgage approval process can take several weeks in Portugal. It involves property appraisal, credit checks, and documentation verification. Timelines may vary depending on the complexity of the application and the lender's efficiency.
